definition.def: A factor is one of the things that affects an event, decision, or situation.
examples: Physical activity is an important factor in maintaining fitness. [+ in]

definition.def: If an amount increases by a factor of two, for example, or by a factor of eight, then it becomes two times bigger or eight times bigger.
examples: The cost of butter quadrupled and bread prices increased by a factor of five. [+ of]

definition.def: You can use factor to refer to a particular level on a scale of measurement.
A factor of a whole number is a smaller whole number which can be multiplied with another whole number to produce the first whole number. [technical]
If you factor a particular cost or element into a calculation you are making, or if you factor it in, you include it. [mainly US]
examples: Using a computer model they factored in the costs of transplants for those women who die. [VERB PARTICLE noun]
You'd better consider this and factor this into your decision making. [VERB noun PARTICLE noun]

examples.sentence: Other factors must be at work and researchers have turned to the brain for clues.
Yet a host of factors pushes employers to hire fewer workers for more hours and, at the same time, compels workers to spend more time on the job.
In business as a whole, there are a number of factors encouraging the prospect of greater equality in the workforce.
Recent research has shown that other factors need to be considered.
There are two key factors behind this trend.
"All these factors must have been necessary but not sufficient to cause the revolution," says Macfarlane.
"There are about 20 different factors and all of them need to be present before the revolution can happen," he says.
"After all, Holland had everything except coal, while China also had many of these factors.
Most historians are convinced there are one or two missing factors that you need to open the lock."
The missing factors, he proposes, are to be found in almost every kitchen cupboard.
